description: Experience the rich, creamy indulgence of classic Butter Chicken, a beloved Indian culinary masterpiece. Tender chicken pieces are simmered in a velvety tomato-based sauce, infused with aromatic spices and finished with a touch of butter and cream. This Murgh Makhani recipe promises an explosion of flavors that will transport your taste buds straight to India.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, 1/2 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, red chili powder, turmeric powder, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, and a pinch of salt. Mix well to coat the chicken. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best results.

instructions.title: Sear the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon butter and 1 tablespoon oil in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until lightly browned. The chicken does not need to be cooked through at this stage. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add another tablespoon of butter. Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped onions and saute until translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1/2 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, green cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Cook for another 2 minutes until fragrant.

instructions.title: Build the Tomato Gravy
instructions.text: Stir in tomato puree and tomato paste. Add cumin powder, coriander powder, the remaining 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, and sugar. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-12 minutes until the sauce thickens and the oil separates from the sides. Add the soaked cashews (drained) to the sauce.

instructions.title: Blend the Sauce
instructions.text: Remove the whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, bay leaf) if desired, or leave them for extra flavor. Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. You may need to add a splash of water (about 1/4 cup) to help it blend. Strain the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an extra silky texture, pressing down on the solids.

instructions.title: Simmer and Finish
instructions.text: Return the pan with the strained sauce to medium-low heat. Add the seared chicken pieces to the sauce. Stir well to combine. Simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and tender, and the flavors have melded. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter, heavy cream, and crushed kasuri methi. Stir until the butter is melted and the sauce is heated through. Do not boil after adding cream.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Taste and adjust salt or sugar if needed. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with naan bread, roti, or basmati rice.

tips: For an extra rich and smoky flavor, you can char the marinated chicken in a tandoor or under a broiler before adding it to the sauce.
Soaking cashews before blending ensures a smoother, creamier sauce and helps prevent grittiness.
Always add cream at the very end and avoid boiling the sauce afterwards to prevent it from splitting.
article:
Butter Chicken, known in its native tongue as Murgh Makhani, is more than just a dish; it's a culinary icon. This beloved Indian chicken recipe has captivated palates worldwide with its rich, creamy texture and tantalizing blend of sweet, tangy, and savory flavors. Originating from the bustling streets of Delhi, Butter Chicken has become a staple in Indian restaurants globally and a cherished meal in countless homes. Its universal appeal lies in its comforting warmth and the harmonious symphony of spices that dance on your tongue. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that restaurant-quality dish in your own kitchen, this comprehensive guide will walk you through every step to achieve the perfect Classic Murgh Makhani.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Its story begins in the 1950s at the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi, where its creators sought to use leftover tandoori chicken in a new, delicious way. The result was a revolutionary dish: tender pieces of chicken simmered in a velvety smooth tomato-based sauce, enriched with butter and cream.

At its heart, Butter Chicken features marinated chicken, traditionally cooked in a tandoor (clay oven), though pan-frying or grilling works perfectly for home cooks. The magic, however, truly lies in its signature sauce. This vibrant, orange-hued gravy is a luxurious blend of ripe tomatoes, fragrant ginger and garlic, and a carefully balanced array of aromatic spices like garam masala and fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi). The addition of butter and fresh cream provides an unparalleled richness, while a touch of sugar or honey balances the acidity of the tomatoes, creating that signature sweet and tangy profile that makes Butter Chicken so irresistible. It's a dish that embodies comfort, warmth, and the soulful essence of Indian cuisine.

## Ingredients for Authentic Butter Chicken

Crafting authentic Butter Chicken requires a selection of fresh, high-quality ingredients. Here's what you'll need:

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri for color, regular for heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice
*   1/2 teaspoon salt

For the Murgh Makhani Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped (optional, for deeper flavor)
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1-2 green chilies, slit (optional, for heat)
*   1 (800g) can crushed tomatoes or 4-5 ripe tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup raw cashews, soaked in warm water for 15-20 minutes
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri)
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 tablespoon garam masala
*   1 teaspoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (or half-and-half)
*   1-2 tablespoons honey or sugar (to taste)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Butter Chicken

Follow these steps to create a show-stopping Butter Chicken at home:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring each piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours, for maximum flavor and tenderness.

2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat a tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary. Sear until lightly charred and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In the same pan, melt the butter over medium heat. If using, add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and green chilies (if using), and cook for another minute until fragrant.

4.  **Build the Flavor:** Stir in the crushed tomatoes or tomato puree. Drain the soaked cashews and add them to the pan. Add the Kashmiri red chili powder, ground cumin, turmeric powder, and garam masala. Mix well and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have reduced and the oil starts to separate from the mixture.

5.  **Achieve Smoothness:** Carefully transfer the cooked sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. For an extra velvety sauce, pass the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan. This step is crucial for that classic restaurant-style texture of Murgh Makhani.

6.  **Simmer and Enrich:** Return the smooth sauce to the pan over low-medium heat. Stir in the crushed kasoori methi. Add the heavy cream and honey or sugar. Mix well and let the sauce gently simmer for 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld beautifully. Taste and adjust salt and sweetness as needed.

7.  **Combine and Serve:** Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering sauce. Stir gently to coat the chicken and cook for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors of the sauce. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro before serving.

## Pro Tips for the Best Murgh Makhani

Achieving restaurant-quality Murgh Makhani at home is entirely possible with a few expert tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't rush the marination process. Longer marination (4+ hours or even overnight) leads to incredibly tender and flavorful chicken. The yogurt helps to tenderize the meat, while the spices infuse it deeply.
*   **Kashmiri Chili Powder:** This specific chili powder is vital for the vibrant red-orange color of Butter Chicken without adding excessive heat. If you can't find it, use regular red chili powder sparingly and add a pinch of food-grade red food coloring for visual appeal.
*   **Kasoori Methi is a Must:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) impart a unique, slightly bitter, and aromatic flavor that is quintessential to Murgh Makhani. Lightly toast them in a dry pan for a few seconds before crushing them between your palms to release their full aroma.
*   **Blend and Strain:** For the smoothest, most luxurious sauce, blending the cooked tomato and cashew mixture thoroughly is essential. Straining it afterwards removes any remaining fibrous bits, giving you that silky texture.
*   **Balance the Flavors:** The perfect Butter Chicken strikes a balance between sweet, tangy, and savory. Don't skip the honey or sugar, as it cuts through the acidity of the tomatoes and rounds out the flavor profile. Taste and adjust to your preference.
*   **Don't Skimp on Butter and Cream:** These are the ingredients that give Butter Chicken its name and its signature richness. Use full-fat dairy for the best results.

## Serving Suggestions for Butter Chicken

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments. Here are some classic serving suggestions:

*   **Indian Breads:** The ultimate pairing for Murgh Makhani is warm, freshly baked naan bread. Garlic naan, butter naan, or plain naan are perfect for scooping up every last drop of the luscious sauce. Roti, chapati, or paratha are also excellent choices.
*   **Rice:** Fragrant basmati rice or jeera rice (cumin-infused rice) provides a comforting base that beautifully complements the rich curry.
*   **Cooling Sides:** A simple raita (yogurt dip with cucumber and mint) or a refreshing kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, and onion with a lemon dressing) offers a delightful contrast to the richness of the Butter Chicken.
*   **Pickles and Chutneys:** A side of mango chutney or a spicy Indian pickle can add an extra layer of flavor and zest to your meal.
*   **Beverages:** A traditional mango lassi (a sweet yogurt drink) is a fantastic way to cool down your palate and complete the authentic Indian dining experience.

## Variations and Substitutions for Butter Chicken

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is perfect as is, there are several ways to adapt it to dietary needs or personal preferences:

*   **Vegetarian Butter Paneer:** Easily transform this dish into a vegetarian delight by substituting the chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese). Simply pan-fry the paneer cubes until golden before adding them to the sauce. Tofu can also be used for a similar effect.
*   **Vegan Murgh Makhani:** For a vegan version, use plant-based butter and full-fat coconut cream instead of dairy butter and heavy cream. Replace the chicken with plant-based chicken substitutes, chickpeas, or roasted cauliflower florets. Ensure your yogurt for marination (if using a plant-based chicken) is also dairy-free.
*   **Spice Level Adjustment:** The heat level of Murgh Makhani is typically mild. If you prefer more spice, increase the amount of red chili powder or add extra green chilies to the sauce. For less heat, reduce or omit the green chilies and use only Kashmiri chili powder.
*   **Healthier Options:** To reduce the calorie count, you can use Greek yogurt in the marinade and opt for a lighter cream or even cashew paste (without the added cream) for richness in the sauce. Reduce the amount of butter, but remember it will slightly alter the classic taste.
*   **Nut-Free Alternative:** If you have a nut allergy, you can substitute the cashews with sunflower seeds or melon seeds, which will still provide thickness, or simply omit them for a slightly thinner sauce. Alternatively, a tablespoon of cornstarch slurry (cornstarch mixed with a little water) can be added at the end to thicken the sauce.

Mastering the art of making Butter Chicken at home is a rewarding culinary journey. With its intoxicating aromas and flavors, this Classic Murgh Makhani is sure to become a cherished recipe in your repertoire, bringing the warmth and richness of Indian cuisine right to your dining table. So gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to indulge in one of the world's most beloved chicken dishes.
